drhp.business: The Group operates through a single segment providing IT support services, and hence no separate segment disclosure is required under Ind AS 108. The Company continues to derive some revenue from its systems integration (SI) business, and management has stated the Company cannot invest in any new businesses or expand current operations, so the business will continue to contract for the foreseeable future.

litigation.note: Multiple legal proceedings and legacy issues are disclosed in the MD&A and Board's Report, including arbitration proceedings against customers to recover overdue receivables on IT support service/system integration contracts, a favorable arbitration award (including interest) received against one customer whose counter claim was disallowed by the Arbitral Tribunal (customer contesting the award), and an MoU for settlement of dues signed with one power project customer and submitted to the Arbitral Tribunal for a consent award. Read in the Management Discussion & Analysis and Board's/Directors' Report sections.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Revenue decline is mainly attributed to the IT support services business on account of completion of certain projects.
- The Company continues to derive some revenue from the systems integration (SI) business.
- IT Support Service Business continues to face delays in certain customers' acceptance and sign-offs on project completion, resulting in delays in recovering receivables.
- Losses are primarily a result of delayed receipts on certain system integration contracts, historical low margin contracts, and large litigations and their costs which are at different stages of progression.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The Group has continuously made losses during past years, its net worth has been fully eroded, and current liabilities exceeded current assets, creating continuity challenges to the Group's 'Going Concern' status.
- Non-cooperation of clients in project sign-off and payments creates disputed billed receivables due to project deliverable issues, delaying recovery of dues.
- Visibility on collections before an Arbitral Award is low, as settlement with Discoms (power distribution company customers) is difficult, and high-value litigation is at different stages of progression.
- Long-term support contracts carry probable failure to comply with contractual commitments due to rapid technological advancements since contract inception, along with uncapped SLA-based penalties.
- Promoter and promoter group have been supporting the Company from time to time by extending loans, corporate guarantees and other financial support; continuity of bank limits depends on this support continuing.
- Risk of loss of human capital in critical operations; management is continuously exploring alternative resourcing including outsourcing to address attrition, with retention plans for identified critical resources.
- Risk of compliance gaps due to operational scale-down, resultant organizational structural changes, and attrition of resources.
- Legacy data resides in older versions of IT applications requiring specialized skills to extract, a skill-set issue arising from organizational downsizing; data retention requirements for the legacy period are regularly reviewed.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Focus on reduction of outstanding debt and losses, continuing actions to help reduce future losses.
- Pursue recovery of long-overdue receivables from customers through arbitration proceedings.
- Maintain continuity of operations to support execution of long-term contracts originally assigned to the Group and support recovery of dues owed to HCL Infotech Limited, following the Scheme of Arrangement transfer of the Hardware Solutions Business.
- The Company cannot invest in any new businesses or in expanding its current operations; the business will continue to contract for the foreseeable future.
